steps.title: Blue is live
steps.caption: Blue runs v1 and serves all traffic. Green, an identical environment, sits idle.
steps.body: **Blue** runs the current version (v1), and the router sends it 100% of production traffic. **Green** is a second production environment, built to match Blue, that serves nothing at the moment. Both environments use the same database.

steps.title: Deploy and test Green
steps.caption: v2 is deployed to Green and smoke-tested through a private test endpoint. Users stay on Blue.
steps.body: The pipeline deploys **v2** to Green while every user stays on Blue. Smoke tests reach Green through a private test endpoint (a preview service, a test listener or a tagged URL) and must pass before anyone switches.

steps.title: Switch
steps.caption: The router sends 100% of traffic to Green in one step. Blue drains and stays warm for rollback.
steps.body: The router points all traffic at Green at once, with a load-balancer target swap, a Kubernetes Service selector change or a DNS record update. Requests already in flight finish on Blue (connection draining), and Blue keeps running, so rolling back is just another switch.

steps.title: Roll back or retire
steps.caption: Errors stay normal, so Blue goes idle and the roles swap. A spike would flip traffic back to Blue.
steps.body: Watch Green's error rate and latency for a while. If they spike, **flip the router straight back** to Blue. If they stay normal, Blue is retired to idle and becomes the target for the next release, so the two environments swap roles with every deployment.
